findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection
findings.evidence: User account credentials (email, password) transmitted to Supabase servers for authentication. AuthService.signIn() at AuthService.ts:16 calls supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({email, password}). AuthService.signUp() at AuthService.ts:28 calls supabase.auth.signUp({email, password}). Supabase client initialized at supabase.ts:12 with URL and anon key from env vars. The bundled index-BMHFFNQZ.js contains bundled Supabase auth-js library (signInWithIdToken, _exchangeCodeForSession, signInWithPassword). Transmission is user-initiated (explicit login/signup button click) to first-party service provider (Supabase).
findings.recommendation: User account data is transmitted to Supabase (first-party service provider) for authentication purposes. This must be declared in the Play Store Data Safety form under 'App functionality' with data type 'Email address' and 'Password'. No prominent in-app disclosure is required as the transmission is user-initiated (Case 3 per evaluation matrix).

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only) - React internal error handler found but no off-device crash reporting SDK (Sentry, Firebase Crashlytics, etc.) is configured. Error is only logged locally via console.error.
findings.evidence: index-BMHFFNQZ.js at byte 38750: React internal polyfill code contains 'process.emit("uncaughtException", e)' followed by 'console.error(e)'. No crash reporting SDK dependencies found in package.json. No google-services.json found. The error handler is React's internal mechanism that logs errors locally via console.error.
findings.recommendation: No immediate action needed. If a crash reporting service (e.g., Firebase Crashlytics, Sentry) is added in the future, the developer must: (1) declare crash log collection in the Play Store Data Safety form, (2) add prominent in-app disclosure with affirmative consent before crash data transmission begins.
findings.purpose: Local error handling only - React internal polyfill

findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection
findings.evidence: Email is collected in three paths: (1) user-provided email during Supabase Auth sign-up/sign-in via index-BMHFFNQZ.js (supabase-js auth client sends email to Supabase Auth endpoint); (2) Google OAuth callback at api/auth/callback.js:34 (tokens.email passed to salvarToken()); (3) stored server-side via api/db.js:43-46 in user_tokens table. All paths are user-initiated (user chooses to sign up or connect Gmail). Destination is the developer's own Supabase/PostgreSQL backend (first party).
findings.recommendation: Declare email collection in Play Store Data Safety form under 'App functionality' with user-initiated flag. No prominent in-app disclosure required since collection is user-initiated.

findings.issue_summary: Manual Sharing
findings.evidence: Full email content (subject, body, recipient, attachment) is transmitted when the user composes and sends an email via api/enviar.js:50 (transporter.sendMail()). The user provides all fields (destinatario, assunto, corpoHtml, pdfBase64) via POST request. The email is relayed through the developer's Vercel server to Gmail API (third-party delivery service chosen by the user). This is a manual sharing action by the user.
findings.recommendation: Policy exempt (manual sharing). No disclosure or Play Store declaration needed. User explicitly triggers the send action with full knowledge of the content being transmitted.

findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: Email data is sent via the backend email-service when the user explicitly triggers email sending. Disclosure exempt per Case 3, but EMAILS must be declared in the Play Store Data Safety form.
findings.evidence: email-service/src/emailService.js lines 37-49: The enviarEmail function sends email data (subject line 'assunto', HTML body 'corpoHtml', recipient 'destinatario', sender name 'remetenteNome', PDF attachment) via Gmail SMTP. Routes defined in routes.js line 70-104 expose POST /enviar accepting userId, destinatario, assunto, corpoHtml, pdfBase64, pdfNome, remetenteNome — all transmitted to the developer's backend and then to Gmail. The user explicitly triggers this action (user fills form and clicks send).
findings.recommendation: Declare EMAILS data collection in the Play Store Data Safety section under 'App functionality'. Since the user initiates the email sending (Case 3), prominent in-app disclosure is exempt, but the data type must be listed in the store listing's Data Safety form.

findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) despite all image handling being user-initiated single-file selection via <input type="file" accept="image/*"> — logo upload, stamp upload, and receipt scanning. TargetSdk=35 makes this a no-op on API 33+, but the broad storage permission is still in the manifest and is unnecessary since the WebView file chooser does not require it.
findings.evidence: Manifest: READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 with maxSdkVersion=32. WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 with maxSdkVersion=28. requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11. Photo usage: SettingsModal.tsx:64 (logo upload, accept="image/*"), SettingsModal.tsx:134 (stamp upload, accept="image/*"), FinanceManager.tsx:267 (receipt scan, accept="image/*" capture="environment"). App is Biz-flow.cloud (business finance app), NOT a dedicated media manager.
findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions from AndroidManifest.xml — the app's image selection flows use <input type="file"> which invokes the system file picker without requiring broad storage permissions on any modern Android version. Remove requestLegacyExternalStorage="true". No functional impact since all image operations are user-initiated and single-file.

findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32), WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=28), and uses requestLegacyExternalStorage=true, but all file operations use Capacitor Filesystem plugin with Directory.Documents (scoped storage on API 30+). No raw file path access found. The permissions are legacy artifacts from pre-scoped-storage era.
findings.evidence: Manifest: requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 (maxSdkVersion=28), READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 (maxSdkVersion=32). main.tsx:31 creates 'Biz-flow/' folder via Capacitor Filesystem mkdir(Directory.Documents). nativeFileService.ts writes/reads PDFs via Capacitor Filesystem to Directory.Documents/Biz-flow/. DocumentShareModal.tsx and useDocumentActions.ts similarly use Capacitor Filesystem scoped API. No direct Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() usage anywhere in the codebase. localStorage reference in assets is browser-level web storage, unrelated to Android file permissions.
findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE from AndroidManifest.xml. Remove android:requestLegacyStorage="true" (only applies to API 29, irrelevant on targetSdk=35). The Capacitor Filesystem plugin already uses scoped storage via the SAF on API 30+ and works correctly without these permissions.

findings.issue_summary: Login screen detected. The app implements a full authentication flow with email/password sign-in, sign-up, password reset, and Google OAuth, gating features behind a user account.
findings.evidence: AuthPage.tsx (lines 60-207) renders a full login/signup/reset UI with email/password form and Google Sign-In button. ConnectAccountModal.tsx (lines 76-182) provides an in-app modal for account connection with Supabase. AuthContext.tsx (lines 40-145) manages auth state and exposes signIn, signUp, signOut, resetPassword, signInWithGoogle. AuthService.ts (lines 13-62) implements actual Supabase Auth API calls (signInWithPassword, signUp, signOut, signInWithOAuth). Users can register and authenticate via email/password or Google.
findings.recommendation: Administrative Console Requirements: Because your app implements a login flow, you MUST complete two manual setup steps in the Play Console dashboard: (1) Submit active, non-expiring test credentials so Google Play reviewers can access gated features. (2) Submit a public-facing web link for account deletion to satisfy Google Play's data deletion policies.

findings.issue_summary: App handles user accounts via Supabase Auth but NO in-app account deletion mechanism exists. The signOut() method only clears the local session without deleting the remote user record.
findings.evidence: AuthContext.tsx lines 99-104: signOut() only calls supabase.auth.signOut() and clears local state (setState({ user: null })) — it does NOT perform a remote account deletion or send a delete/purge API call. AuthService.ts lines 38-42: signOut() calls supabase.auth.signOut() and logs warnings but never triggers account deletion. No file in the codebase contains any account deletion code (searched for 'deleteAccount', 'delete_account', 'apagar.conta', 'removeAccount', 'deletar', 'remove account'). No Profile or Settings pages exist where a deletion option could be placed.
findings.recommendation: Implement in-app deletion: Create a highly discoverable path (e.g., under User Profile / Account Settings) to let users initiate account deletion directly in the app. The deletion must call a Supabase Admin API or Edge Function to permanently remove the user's remote database records, not merely sign them out.
